subject: chemistry
question_text: Define atomic number and mass number.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Atomic number
lines: Atomic number (Z): the number of protons
present in the nucleus of an atom.
In a neutral atom it is also the number of
steps.why: The proton count is what fixes the element, so the atomic number is the identity of the atom. The electron count matches it only while the atom is neutral, which is why that condition is stated.
common_mistakes: Defining the atomic number as the number of electrons without the word neutral. An ion has a different electron count.
Confusing Z with the mass number.
steps.memory_tip: Z counts protons. Protons decide which element it is.
steps.margin_note: Give the symbol Z along with the definition.

steps.label: Mass number

lines.text: Mass number A = number of protons + number of neutrons

lines: Protons and neutrons together are called
nucleons, so A is the number of nucleons.
steps.why: Almost all the mass of an atom sits in the nucleus, so counting the nucleons gives the mass number. Writing A − Z for the neutrons shows the two definitions working together.
common_mistakes: Including the electrons in the mass number. Their mass is too small to count.
Writing the mass number as the atomic mass in grams. A is a whole-number count.
steps.memory_tip: A counts everything in the nucleus. Subtract Z and the neutrons are left.
steps.margin_note: The line neutrons = A − Z is worth adding. It costs one line.
